purpose: Replacement title illustrations following user rejection of v1. Illustrative metaphors, not historical evidence or factual model architecture.

references.role: Opera singer identity and Pop-Art style

prompts:
Use case: stylized-concept. Generate a NEW portrait illustration for the complete left image column of an academic slide. Aspect ratio exactly 4:5. The attached slide is a CHARACTER AND PRINT-STYLE reference only; reproduce neither the full slide nor any title text. CRITICAL: the ONLY human character is the SAME OPERA SINGER WOMAN seen on the LEFT of the reference: the same recognizable face, waved short dark hair, distinctive ornate opera tiara/headdress, drop earrings, pearl necklace, fur-trimmed black-and-white stage costume. NO MAN. NO modern researcher, eyeglasses, office outfit, laptop scene, second person or extra human face. Match the reference's precise bold rough black ink print, stark black-white contrast, coarse Ben-Day halftone dots, angular comic flashes, expressive vintage opera illustration. Sparse deep purple #632b8a accents; no other colors. 
Layout: full portrait single framed image. Upper roughly 55%: this opera singer in a strong half-length portrait, facing toward the lower-right, curious but skeptical, one hand holding a manuscript sheet at waist level. Preserve her face and extravagant stage attire closely. Lower roughly 45%: a FEW large clear conceptual objects on white background. At left an old source letter and a simple prompt speech bubble filled only with three black horizontal strokes. They feed by short purple arrows into the central LLM BLACK BOX: an opaque irregular black angular core, like a jagged alien object with 4–6 long, thin, sharp, segmented, tentacle-like appendages. It is unmistakably foreign and inscrutable, not cute, not a round octopus, not a robot, not a neutral node-network icon, no visible mechanism inside. One angular tentacle releases a generated page to the right. On that output page some lines end as broken fragments, with a single floating question-mark symbol above, to communicate uncertainty. Keep the drawing conceptual; no claims of factual output. Clear hierarchy, enough white space between objects, black box is the focal point of the lower section. Small purple directional arrows only. A diagonal comic-panel divider may separate portrait and technical content as in reference. Thin purple outer frame. No title, captions, branding, watermark, readable words, numbers or decorative pseudotext. The ONLY allowed printed symbol is one question mark.

Edit IMAGE 1 (the portrait pop-art opera singer illustration), preserving its exact dimensions, purple frame, upper singer portrait, costume, face, all dots, white space, panel divider and overall composition. Only modify TWO objects in the lower panel. First: replace the central star-shaped black object with a BLACK CUBE HEAD with two tiny white dots, inspired by the creature in IMAGE 2 (motif reference only). The cube has an opaque black interior, crisp angular outline, subtle white edge lines; below it a short black body connects to several jagged, bent, alien tentacles, keeping the same footprint as the prior object. Translate the motif into the rough black-white halftone ink print of IMAGE 1; do not use blue, watercolor, glossy 3D or a human/robot body. Preserve the purple input/output arrows, their direction and space. Second: replace the musical notation on the lower RIGHT output page with clearly typeset prose represented by grouped short horizontal black lines of varied length, no musical staff, no notes, no readable words. Retain its disintegrating uncertain line endings and the question mark above. The singer's held MUSIC manuscript remains untouched. The input source letter and prompt speech bubble remain untouched. ONLY ONE HUMAN, the same opera singer. No new title, caption, labels or icons.
images.visualReview: One opera singer with tiara, pearls, drop earrings and fur stage costume; opaque cube with jagged tentacles; source and prompt inputs; generated prose lines with uncertain endings and question mark. No extra human or modern researcher.

prompts:
Generate one complete PORTRAIT 4:5 illustration for the left column of an academic title slide. IMAGE 1 is the original character and exact Pop-Art print-style reference: use ONLY its opera singer, NOT the man and NOT the slide text. IMAGE 2 is the approved companion composition and alien motif: match its palette, line weight, dot pattern, frame and opera-singer identity. IMAGE 3 is the alien black-box motif reference only, do not copy its blue/watercolor style.
THE ONLY HUMAN ANYWHERE must be the SAME recognizable OPERA SINGER from Image1: waved short dark hair, ornate opera tiara/headdress, drop earrings, pearl necklace, fur-trimmed shoulder-baring stage costume, expressive vintage face; no glasses, no modern researcher, no man, no miniature human icons. Same stark black-white coarse Ben-Day halftone rough ink print, sparse dark-purple #632b8a accents. No soft shading, glossy 3D, stock photography, modern office or laptop scene.
Upper 55–60%: opera singer in a confident half-length pose, slight smile, looking DOWN toward her work. She holds an old music manuscript in her left hand; her right hand extends with a magnifying glass across the diagonal panel division to CHECK a tiny research-tool window below. Keep both hands anatomically clear.
Lower 40–45%: clean few-element conceptual composition on white. LEFT: one small stack of source/context cards, top card has handwritten squiggles and small musical marks. Short purple arrow feeds these into the CENTRAL alien black box: opaque BLACK CUBE HEAD with thin white edges and two tiny white dots, short body made from black ink and coarse halftone, uneven jagged angular tentacles like Image2 (NOT a neutral network icon). One tentacle manipulates a small bracket/code card; another reaches a simple research-tool browser window on RIGHT. That single window clearly contains two schematic panes: tiny source page and structured table. No real software screenshot, no readable labels, only a few clean lines. The singer's magnifying glass is over the tool/source area, making her direct verification visually explicit. ONE purple feedback arrow bends from the checked tool window BACK toward the black cube. Convey: contextual sources + opaque agent using code/tool + human checking + feedback. DO NOT draw multiple computers, multiple windows, extra icons, extra humans, robots, brains, puzzle pieces, charts, decorative gears or unnecessary arrows. Alien is a conceptual metaphor, not a real technical architecture. Entire image contains no title, captions, readable words, logos, watermarks or numbers. Thin purple frame. Strong calm layout visible at thumbnail size; leave white space between lower elements.

Edit the supplied illustration with EXACTLY ONE geometric correction: the large purple curved arrow at the very bottom currently points from the black tentacled cube toward the browser window. REVERSE that arrow so it points from the browser window BACK TOWARD THE BLACK CUBE, forming a clear feedback loop. Keep the same arc shape and approximate location, but its arrowhead must be at the LEFT end nearest the cube/tentacles, and its plain tail at the RIGHT end below the browser window. Do not change any other pixels or elements: opera singer's face, tiara, costume, hands and magnifying glass; source cards; opaque cube with two dots and angular tentacles; code card; browser window; panel divider; all sizes, lines, colors, dots, purple frame and portrait dimensions. No new arrows or objects.
images.visualReview: Same opera singer only; sources/context input; opaque cube with jagged tentacles operating code and source/table tool; singer holds magnifying glass for review; feedback arrow points from tool back to agent.

validationScope: Generated assets only. Native-slide integration delegated to parent agent.
